rule_1_durability.consequence: the measurement an incident most needs is the one an incident most easily loses.  A null peak means NOT MEASURED; it never means small
rule_1_durability.observed: shard 1 and shard 2 failed identically, seconds apart in CPU terms.  Shard 1 released cleanly and kept 3540209664 B.  Shard 2 was reclaimed and kept nothing
rule_1_durability.proposed: have the monitor persist its running peak into the lease as it samples, so a reclaim inherits the last sample instead of null
rule_1_durability.statement: the whole-cgroup peak is written back into the lease ONLY BY A SUCCESSFUL RELEASE.  If the launcher's bounded drain loop does not succeed -- a descendant still in the scope, a core being written -- it correctly leaves the reservation held rather than handing its bytes to a second admission, and the sweep reclaims it later as LEASE_RECLAIMED_WITNESS_DEAD with observed_peak_bytes null

rule_2_resolution.consequence: a cap is sized from the LARGER of the whole-cgroup peak and the main-process peak unless the child was long enough to be sampled; every cap declared in this round was sized that way
rule_2_resolution.observed: the same GPU smoke child reported 90726400 B when it ran for 1.6 s and 576438272 B when given a dwell, against a main-process RSS peak of 967823360 B in both
rule_2_resolution.state: a property of the sampler, recorded so no number here is read as more than it is
rule_2_resolution.statement: for a child that lives less than the monitor's sampling interval the whole-cgroup peak is a FLOOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT
